sources.title: Robustness of slow contraction to cosmic initial conditions
sources.authors: A. Ijjas, W. G. Cook, F. Pretorius, P. J. Steinhardt, G. N. Davies
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: numerical-relativity simulations vary all freely specifiable initial data (shear, curvature, scalar-field and velocity profiles), including data far outside the perturbative regime, and find slow contraction robust. A follow-up (arXiv:2104.12293) reports robustness enhanced with several modes and reduced symmetry. The evolution formulation and its constraint-damping choices are not stated in the record.
sources.relevance: A template: test whether the two Chat 14 fates survive non-perturbative disturbances rather than the narrow balanced two-bump family. Arbitrary data first need a constraint solve. The programme's discrete-constraint projection (evolution_constraints workstream) is the analogue of that step.

sources.title: Characteristic evolution of conformal scattering: I. Scalar Waves in Minkowski Spacetime
sources.authors: He, Tian and Zhang (surnames as recorded)
sources.finding: Per the programme record: studies compactified double-null scattering with alternative characteristic stencils, and reports loss of convergence near spatial infinity. Its stability, convergence and Richardson-extrapolation evidence are numerical, not interval certificates.
sources.relevance: A compactified or characteristic outer region is one way to stop the far-boundary signals that contaminate the late Chat 14 values (H/H0 near 0.628690 arrives after taper and boundary signals could reach the shell). The reported loss of convergence at the compactified edge is a warning to test any such map with a convergence study at the new boundary.

sources.title: A posteriori error analysis and adaptivity of a space-time finite element method for the wave equation in second order formulation
sources.authors: Dong, Georgoulis, Mascotto and Wang (surnames as recorded)
sources.venue: arXiv:2509.08537v2; Numerische Mathematik, DOI 10.1007/s00211-026-01561-3 (per programme record)
sources.finding: Per the programme record: explicit a posteriori error bounds from temporal and spatial reconstructions, including mesh-change discontinuities, for a scalar wave equation on a bounded domain.
sources.relevance: a route from 'grid convergence' to computable error estimates for wave evolutions. The HDBLAST system (coupled, nonlinear, with a shell boundary) would need its own constants. At most it can guide an error indicator near the steep wall.

sources.title: BRANECODE: A Program for Simulations of Braneworld Dynamics
sources.authors: J. Martin, G. Felder, A. Frolov, M. Peloso, L. Kofman (per sweep-1 record)
sources.venue: arXiv:hep-ph/0404141; companion 'Brane world dynamics with the BraneCode', arXiv:hep-th/0309001
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a C++ code for fully nonlinear evolution of 5D braneworlds with bulk scalar fields, described as the first of its type, used to confirm the tachyonic instability of 'stabilized' de Sitter branes. The programme's Chat 9 prior-art file (which read the papers through ar5iv on 16 Sept 2026) gives hep-th/0309001 as the BraneCode reference; the two identifiers may be a program paper and a dynamics paper, which this sweep could not check.
sources.relevance: the closest published analogue of rolloff5d (nonlinear 5D evolution of a brane with bulk scalar and junction conditions). Reproducing one published BraneCode test would give the programme an external calibration that its internal controls cannot provide.

sources.title: Dynamics of Anti-de Sitter Domain Walls
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: moving domain walls in the Randall-Sundrum universe with the bulk patched from AdS5 black-hole solutions; the junction equations fix the wall motion, which observers on the wall see as cosmological expansion or contraction.
sources.relevance: an exact moving-shell benchmark. A thin shell in pure AdS5 (scalar frozen at a vacuum) evolved by the HDBLAST moving-boundary code must reproduce the exact Friedmann-type trajectory, including the a^-4 bulk-mass term when a black-hole patch is used. This tests the shell closure separately from the scalar physics.

sources.title: When do colliding bubbles produce an expanding universe?
sources.authors: J. J. Blanco-Pillado and colleagues (per sweep-1 record)
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a symmetric collision leaves a collapsing universe unless the bulk expansion rate before the collision is large compared with the momentum transfer in the fifth dimension; thick-wall numerical collisions confirm the thin-wall result.
sources.relevance: a published thin-wall versus thick-wall numerical cross-validation, the check HDBLAST needs if the Israel shell is ever replaced by a resolved wall. P4: an explicit expansion-versus-collapse criterion to evaluate along the Chat 14 trajectories.

sources.title: Dynamics of colliding branes and black brane production
sources.authors: Y. Takamizu, H. Kudoh, K. Maeda
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: self-gravitating colliding domain walls (initial data from a BPS wall in 5D supergravity) generically form a spacelike curvature singularity covered by a horizon, a black brane with trapped walls; non-relativistic weak-field cases can pass through or bounce.
sources.relevance: a concrete hypothesis and a method for the unconverged Chat 14 collapse: track trapped surfaces. In the 1+1 reduction with metric e^{2B}(-dt^2+dz^2)+e^{2A}dx_3^2, a trapped region is where (d_t+d_z)A and (d_t-d_z)A are both negative. Evaluating this needs the velocity-field snapshots the Chat 14 archive lacks, so it must be added to new runs.

sources.title: Crunch from AdS bubble collapse in unbounded potentials
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: an AdS bubble nucleated in a Minkowski false vacuum, in a potential with an infinitely deep true vacuum, has an interior that collapses to a spacelike singularity behind an apparent horizon; trapped surfaces form once kinetic energy dominates.
sources.relevance: the diagnostic set for the collapse fate: apparent-horizon location, trapped-surface formation, and the sign of the local energy density. The registered U is also unbounded below (sweep 1 checked U ~ -(2/27) phi^6 exactly).

sources.title: Simulating the universe(s) II: phenomenology of cosmic bubble collisions in full General Relativity
sources.authors: Johnson, Peiris, Lehner and collaborators (per query context in sweep 1)
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: full-GR simulations of bubble collisions that compute cosmological observables directly from the scalar Lagrangian, giving relativistic predictions that differ significantly from non-relativistic approximations.
sources.relevance: established practice for evolving resolved scalar walls in full GR in a symmetry-reduced setting. It is an alternative to a thin Israel shell, and a later route from a violent 5D event to observables.

sources.title: Exactly solvable model for cosmological perturbations in dilatonic brane worlds
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a bulk scalar with exponential potential and exponential coupling to the brane tension gives power-law inflation on a single brane; the backreacted background and the perturbations obeying the junction conditions are solved exactly.
sources.relevance: an exact benchmark with a bulk scalar, a moving de Sitter-like brane and both junction conditions. It is the cheapest external test of the full perturbation and junction machinery.

sources.title: Perturbations on domain walls and strings: A covariant theory
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a covariant perturbation formalism for walls and strings, including nucleated bubbles and walls in de Sitter space; the perturbation field often has a tachyonic mass and a nonminimal coupling to worldsheet curvature, and, without gravity, one scalar describes wall translations.
sources.relevance: the standard way to separate wall-translation (gauge) modes from physical instabilities. This round's gauge-invariant stability workstream already classifies the mu^2 = -4 harmonics on the +1 branch as pure gauge in the bulk.

sources.title: Brane-world creation and black holes
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: an inflating brane-world can be created from nothing with its AdS bulk; the de Sitter brane instanton has AdS inside; 5D and 4D actions and entropies agree when the instanton is much larger than the AdS radius; thermal instantons with a bulk AdS black hole may describe creation of a hot universe.
sources.relevance: the Euclidean static branch (an S^4 shell bounding a hyperbolic 5-ball, Z2-doubled) is this instanton with a bulk scalar. If the branch is to be read as a tunnelling or creation saddle, its negative-mode count must be computed. The Lorentzian stability result of this round does not settle that count.

sources.title: Can Inflating Braneworlds be Stabilized?
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: for de Sitter branes the radion mass squared is typically negative, confirmed with BraneCode numerics. The programme's Chat 9 file (full text read via ar5iv, 16 Sept 2026) adds: scalar perturbations in generalized longitudinal gauge reduce to a self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville problem with a Rayleigh bound m^2 <= -4H^2 + (2/3) int(dw/a) / int(dw/(a phi'^2)), and the programme reproduced its registered eigenvalue mu^2 = -7.7178716 with these equations.
sources.relevance: because the problem is self-adjoint Sturm-Liouville, rigorous eigenvalue enclosures of the kind found in verification-method texts (E2) apply in principle. The +1-branch statement 'no normalizable scalar mode below 9/4' could be certified rather than only computed.

sources.title: Radion on the de Sitter brane
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: with two de Sitter branes of opposite tension the radion has negative mass squared proportional to the brane curvature; with a single positive-tension de Sitter brane there is no radion.
sources.relevance: fixes which scalar modes can exist with one shell and a regular cone.

sources.title: Thick Brane Worlds and Their Stability
sources.authors: S. Kobayashi, K. Koyama, J. Soda
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: non-singular thick Poincare, de Sitter and AdS branes with a dilaton have positive-definite effective potentials in their scalar master equations, hence stability.
sources.relevance: a master-variable (Schrodinger-form) method. A positive-definite effective potential would be an analytic stability proof, stronger than a numerical spectrum.

sources.title: Fake supergravity and domain wall stability
sources.authors: D. Z. Freedman, C. Nunez, M. Schnabl, K. Skenderis
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a generalized Witten-Nester spinor argument proves stability of flat domain walls without supersymmetry in any dimension, extended to AdS-sliced walls.
sources.relevance: covers the balanced flat wall (delta = 0) only. The record shows no analogous positive-energy theorem for de Sitter-sliced walls, so +1-branch stability has to be computed, or proved by a new argument.

sources.title: Hidden Supersymmetry of Domain Walls and Cosmologies
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: every domain-wall solution with Minkowski or AdS worldvolume admits first-order equations with a solution-determined superpotential; FLRW cosmologies obey similar equations through pseudo-Killing spinors.
sources.relevance: a first-order reformulation reduces the static BVP to a lower-order system, which is often the key simplification in a computer-assisted proof. The de Sitter-sliced case needs the curved version.

sources.title: Coupled bulk and brane fields about a de Sitter brane
sources.authors: A. Cardoso, K. Koyama, A. Mennim, S. S. Seahra, D. Wands
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: a bulk scalar coupled linearly to a scalar on a de Sitter brane has zero, one or two bound states plus resonances; with brane test-field matter an infinite ladder of discrete tachyonic modes can become normalizable.
sources.relevance: any matter extension that couples a shell field to phi needs a coupled-sector negative-mode check. Adding brane fields can create normalizable tachyons that the vacuum analysis cannot see.

sources.title: Complex scalar field thick branes: stability of linear perturbation and evolution of scalar Kaluza-Klein modes coupled with gravity
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: Minkowski, de Sitter and AdS thick branes from a complex scalar show no instability in the scalar and vector sectors; a factorized tensor equation excludes tachyonic tensor modes.
sources.relevance: a current sector-by-sector template, including the vector sector, which this round's stability workstreams did not treat.

sources.title: Revisiting Coleman-de Luccia transitions in the AdS regime using holography
sources.authors: J. K. Ghosh, E. Kiritsis, F. Nitti, L. T. Witkowski
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: CDL AdS-to-AdS decays in Einstein-scalar theories are interpreted as vev-driven holographic RG flows on de Sitter space; such flows do not exist for generic potentials, and existence is tied to exotic RG flows.
sources.relevance: existence of de Sitter-sliced regular solutions is non-generic, so an existence proof for the +1 branch is not a formality. P2: gives the tunnelling interpretation in which a negative-mode count matters.

sources.title: Searching for Coleman-de Luccia bubbles in AdS compactifications
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: fully backreacted instantons are obtained by numerically integrating first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations for smooth de Sitter-foliated walls between AdS vacua.
sources.relevance: an independent solver architecture (first-order Hamilton-Jacobi) for the same class of solutions; a cross-check on the +1 branch that shares no code with the checkpoint's shooting solvers.

sources.title: Holographic RG flows on curved manifolds and quantum phase transitions
sources.authors: J. K. Ghosh, E. Kiritsis, F. Nitti, L. T. Witkowski
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: Einstein-dilaton flows with dS, AdS or sphere slicing and general potential; UV and IR asymptotics; new flows at finite curvature with no flat counterpart.
sources.relevance: the regular-endpoint (IR) expansions classified there are the local cone solutions a certification needs. In this problem the linear germ is the explicit polynomial C_14^(2)(cosh u) (pilot, part 1).

sources.title: Generalized surface tension bounds in vacuum decay
sources.authors: A. Masoumi, S. Paban, E. J. Weinberg
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: defines a tension for thin walls whose curvature radius changes across the wall and derives CDL-like bounds for bounces with Minkowski or AdS false vacua.
sources.relevance: context for tunnelling interpretations of a shell with a nonconstant scalar profile.

sources.title: Gravitational Effects on and of Vacuum Decay
sources.year: 1980 (per sweep-1 caveat, year from general knowledge)
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: gravity can prevent decay of a Minkowski or AdS false vacuum; in the thin-wall limit this happens above a tension bound.
sources.relevance: origin of the CDL setting in which the 'negative-mode problem' arises. The negative-mode literature itself (Lavrelashvili, Lee-Weinberg, Koehn-Lavrelashvili-Lehners and others) could not be retrieved in this sweep; see LEADS.

sources.authors: not stated in the programme record
sources.finding: Per the programme record: the established instant-preheating benchmark, adapted there to a brane field with m_eff^2 = m_chi^2 + g_b^2 (phi - phi_*)^2 crossing linearly: n_k = exp[-pi (k^2 + m_chi^2)/mu^2], n_chi = mu^3/(8 pi^3) exp[-pi m_chi^2/mu^2], mu^2 = g_b |phi_dot_b|, in the locally flat adiabatic in/out limit. sources.title: A dynamical inflaton coupled to strongly interacting matter

sources.relevance: the only item in this session's records that computes reheating with full self-consistent backreaction; the heat bath is a 5D (holographic) sector. Methodologically the closest template for bulk-coupled feedback, which this round's preheating workstream did not solve.

sources.title: Gravitational reheating at strong coupling

sources.relevance: an upper-bound method for gravitational production during a change of de Sitter rate.

sources.title: Reheating the Universe in Braneworld Cosmological Models with bulk-brane energy transfer
sources.finding: Per the sweep-1 snippet record: analyses the reheating era in 5D braneworlds with brane-bulk energy exchange.
sources.relevance: a precedent for the energy-exchange law of the programme's matter extension.

sources.title: Computer-assisted construction of SU(2)-invariant negative Einstein metrics
sources.finding: Per the programme record: high-accuracy approximate solutions, rigorous residual bounds and a fixed-point argument yield actual Riemannian Einstein metrics, with explicit constants and reproducible computations.
sources.relevance: the closest structural precedent found. The Euclidean continuation of the +1 branch is a symmetry-reduced (cohomogeneity-one) Riemannian Einstein-scalar metric on a ball with a regular centre and an S^4 shell boundary. The Riemannian approximation -> residual -> fixed-point architecture therefore applies more directly to the static branch than to any Lorentzian evolution. The static Lorentzian problem is the same ODE BVP.

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Gundlach, Calabrese, Hinder, Martin-Garcia (2005): constraint damping in the Z4 formulation and harmonic gauge
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Damping terms that drive constraint violations to zero at a tunable rate. The direct remedy for the outgoing constraint front (P3).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Alic, Bona-Casas, Bona, Rezzolla, Palenzuela (2012): conformal and covariant Z4 (CCZ4)
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Standard damped formulation used in spherical and higher-dimensional codes (P3, P4).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Bernuzzi, Hilditch (2010): Z4c; and later work on constraint-preserving boundary conditions for Z4c
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Constraint-preserving outer boundaries, the other half of the far-boundary problem (P3).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Pretorius (2005) and Lindblom, Scheel, Kidder, Owen, Rinne (2006): generalized harmonic evolution with constraint damping
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Alternative damped formulation; widely used for AdS and cosmological problems (P3, P4).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Zenginoglu (2008): hyperboloidal foliations and scri-fixing; later hyperboloidal spherical-symmetry work
leads_unverified_no_url.why: P3: in the evolution chart the far end of the bulk (z -> -infinity) is the Lorentzian continuation of the regular cone. That is a Rindler-type horizon of the de Sitter slicing, reached only asymptotically in coordinate time. Horizon-penetrating or hyperboloidal-type slices would let outgoing signals leave instead of reflecting from a finite boundary.

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Sarbach, Tiglio (2012), Living Reviews in Relativity: continuum and discrete initial-boundary value problems and Einstein's equations
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Well-posed boundary conditions and summation-by-parts (SBP) discretizations with energy estimates (P3, P5).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Summation-by-parts operators with simultaneous-approximation-term (SAT) boundary and interface closures (review literature on SBP-SAT)
leads_unverified_no_url.why: P5: Chat 14 found that the order of the one-sided shell closure dominated the error at delta=0.001. SBP-SAT closures give provably stable boundary/interface treatments of a chosen order.

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Higher-dimensional numerical relativity with symmetry reduction (modified cartoon method, Shibata-Yoshino; 5D CCZ4 codes)
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Established 5D formulations if the programme leaves the 1+1 reduction (P3).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Chesler, Yaffe (2014): characteristic formulation for asymptotically AdS gravitational dynamics
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Characteristic (null) evolution in AdS5 avoids an artificial timelike outer boundary (P3, P4).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Israel (1966): singular hypersurfaces and thin shells; Ida (2000): brane-world cosmology from junction conditions
leads_unverified_no_url.why: Foundations for the moving-shell benchmarks (P5).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Lavrelashvili (2006) and Lee, Weinberg (2014): negative modes of Coleman-De Luccia bounces
leads_unverified_no_url.why: The CDL negative-mode problem: counting and gauge-invariant definition of the negative mode (P2).

leads_unverified_no_url.pointer: Koehn, Lavrelashvili, Lehners (2015): towards a solution of the negative-mode problem in quantum tunnelling with gravity
